A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 40 pages of each, including Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original numerical optimization and simulations, including FICO-initialized agent populations, parameter sweeps, and robustness experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations and optimization outcomes, including Tables 5.1–5.2 and the experimental figures in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The promotion/abstention/relegation model, objectives, greedy threshold construction in Algorithm 1, and interpolated value iteration in Algorithm 2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the FICO score distribution to initialize simulated agents and retain the same synthetic parameter scenarios and alternative leg-up settings. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario changes.

E2.justification: The binary promote/relegate comparator in Appendix E.5 and Figure 16 remains unchanged, as does the oracle reference in Table 5.2. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Data normalization, parameter settings, metrics, and numerical evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix E.3.1 retains the CMA-ES population size of 10 and 30-iteration limit.

E4.justification: Both retain the same parameter ablations, alternative leg-up tests, misspecification study, binary-versus-ternary analysis, and grid/truncation sensitivity tests in Section 5 and Appendices D.3 and E.

E5.justification: Figures 13–14 retain their mean trajectories and plus/minus one standard-deviation reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 5.1 retains utilities of 630.4 for Case I and 107.9 for Case IV; Table 5.2 and the appendix result figures also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, propositions, theorems, equations, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Theorem 5.1 moves between pages; capitalization and footnote-number edits do not alter mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about sequential incentives, optimal agent strategies, and arbitrarily high attainment through honest improvement under the stated conditions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retention, farsightedness, leg-up effects, failure regimes, and applicability limits are unchanged. The added clause in Section 6 redundantly repeats an existing explanation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code-availability statement and GitHub repository link absent from v2. Existing implementation details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information but do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion in Appendix A, and positioning relative to earlier strategic-classification research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 6 loses a colon and gains a redundant, malformed trailing clause; Appendix C.4.1 changes 'we' to 'We'. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new first-page footnote causes limited column and page reflow, including moving Theorem 5.1 from page 6 to page 7. Figures and tables retain their designs and captions.

improvement.justification: The new code link supplies an implementation-access pointer missing from v2, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. This limited benefit outweighs the small editorial regression from Section 6's duplicated clause. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged, and code completeness cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
